links.outcome: Patient attitudes, trust, and usage intentions under proactive (ethics committee, audits, explanations, feedback) vs passive ethics practices
links.effect: Proactive vs passive: attitudes M=5.67 vs 4.28 (F(1,504)=154.677, p<.001); trust M=5.57 vs 4.31 (F=141.976, p<.001); usage intention M=5.37 vs 4.14 (reported p<.084).
links.quote: Proactive algorithmic ethics practices significantly increased positive attitudes, trust, and usage intentions compared to passive practices.

links.effect: Proactive vs passive ethics practices improved attitudes: M=5.67, SD=1.00 vs M=4.28, SD=1.52; F(1, 504)=154.677, p<.001.
links.quote: Participants exposed to proactive algorithmic ethics practices reported more favorable attitudes toward the healthcare provider (M = 5.67, SD = 1.00) than those exposed to passive practices (M = 4.28, SD = 1.52).
